scoreNotes.shapeVolume: Clear native improvement from the source blank prism and cubic moss: rounded planted moss masses, a weathered shoulder, visible crown ledge and carved fractures. The column remains more regular than the target.
scoreNotes.color: Warm pale ivory remains dominant, with distinct olive/lime moss and subdued cream-gray stone variation. The source cyan cast and fluorescent green blocks are resolved.
scoreNotes.lightingHighlights: Soft broad native response holds stone and moss color in every facing; no white blowout or preferred horizontal light direction. Volume is gentler and less dramatically separated than the painted target.
scoreNotes.materialDetail: Native groove depth and soft bevels remain readable. The design uses simpler weathering and fracture construction than the target, with restrained noise rather than painted surface accents.
scoreNotes.artifactFreeReadability: All four registered views read as broken pale columns at logical size, including the real browser consumer; edges, grounding and major details hold without material defects.

observations: The fixed target is used as an aesthetic design reference, not as registration evidence. Original snapshot, fixed target and independently measured source contract were inspected before editor proposals in the initial review.

N/E/S/W native PNGs were directly inspected, along with all published candidate renders and every required preview. Exact pixel comparison proves that the four-view, logical and background contact sheets are unmodified whole-canvas composites of these render bytes.

Warm ivory/cream stone replaces the original broad cyan-gray wash. Crown and base remain lightly varied rather than featureless white, while the moss reads as rounded organic volume with muted lime/olive shading.

The wide square plinth and rounded shoulder support the shaft. Native crown ledges, diagonal fracture recesses and small settled stone forms establish a broken weathered column. The strong dark gray fracture strokes have visible edge thickness; their simplified recurring pattern is accepted as a coherent four-sided design.

All four views preserve a clear column silhouette and coherent native model rotation. Crown moss placement changes with facing; repeated lower-side motifs are actual native geometry, not per-view image fitting.

At logical 192x320 size, crown moss, long shaft fractures and the substantial foot stay legible. Light, neutral gray and dark composites show clean alpha, no clipping, unwanted ground shadow, broad black dead spots or material floating/overlap defects.

The native images contain only 0-3 opaque near-black pixels per facing, at the tiny occluded tip under the right-side moss, not a visible black patch at intended size. This local crevice occlusion is non-blocking; the rest of the fracture recesses retain gray value.

Repeated and related-submarine context show grounded one-cell supports at fixed pitch. Tall rear columns are naturally occluded by front rows. There are no sockets or port profiles, so seamless structural joins are not imposed.

The judge independently ran the actual #object-column-broken SpriteScene at desktop1440x1000, phone390x844 and landscape844x390. All four-facing/repeated/interaction scenes were raster-ready, with exact sealed candidate atlas responses, no page errors and no document-width overflow.
remainingDifferences: The native foot is a single weathered square plinth with a shoulder and restrained stone chips, rather than the target layered broken masonry. It remains substantial, grounded and within the functional footprint.

The shaft and crown are more regular, with shallower crown variation and simpler repeated angular fractures than the target. Those native forms still communicate the broken-column identity and improve the source model within the approved design freedom.

Surface variation and moss detailing are softer and less contrasty than the painted target. Fine painted mottling and the target exact crack map are not necessary for readability at the registered size.
The light is horizontally symmetric and gentler than the target one-sided warm highlight, as required for the rotatable world.

independentNativeAudit.method: Direct background Blender inspection of sealed source, including actual vertex bounds, camera, resources, materials, lights, drivers/actions and bmesh topology.
independentNativeAudit.topology: All19 meshes closed manifold, no zero-area faces, positive signed volumes.
independentNativeAudit.rasterSubstitute: No file images, linked libraries or raster shader nodes. No armature/actions/drivers.
independentNativeAudit.lighting: One centered overhead plus four equal cardinal fills; no mesh outside asset collection or directional ground-shadow receiver.

independentPortableReplay.method: Relocated copy containing only exact source/round-03.blend and replay-round-03.py; four fresh Blender native renders written inside reviews/. Replay script read and checked for source-only dependency closure.
independentPortableReplay.captureContract: Single fixed camera; native source facing rotation precedes canonical .42-transition square-footing Y warp; no per-view fitting/recoloring/regrading.
independentPortableReplay.limits: Decoded RGBA equality is the reproducibility criterion; PNG metadata bytes may differ. No Godot shipping integration is claimed.

actualBrowser.candidateURLBinding: Same-origin production image redirects to hash-tagged sealed candidate atlas URLs; response bytes independently hashed. No production file change.
actualBrowser.scopeLimit: Actual browser consumer inspected. Column is outside current Godot restaurant selection; no unused Godot bench or shipping claim.

approvalScope: Only the exact packet-bound round03 source and renders. This verdict does not authorize unrelated production or publishing changes.
